output.research_question: How do writers in these fictional posts describe pressures and resources that shape their current experience of stress?
output.analysis_summary: In these fictional posts, stress is described as arising from overlapping demands on time, money, care, safety, and responsibility, while relief appears through routines, practical help, boundaries, humor, planning, or a resolved administrative problem. Several excerpts also mark partial relief: a resource can make one evening breathable or a joke can help without removing the underlying strain.

codes.label: Stacked time pressure
codes.definition: Multiple duties or deadlines compete for limited time and attention.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when an excerpt names deadlines, appointments, jobs, transport, moves, or recurring questions as time or attention demands.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for financial scarcity alone unless it is tied to attention or scheduling pressure.

exemplars.quote: Three deadlines landed in the same week.
arranging my father's appointments while trying to keep a new job

codes.label: Material insecurity
codes.definition: Basic resources such as rent, shelter, food, transport, or utilities are uncertain or inadequate.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the excerpt directly names bills, rent, groceries, shelter, elevator access, or similar material constraints.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for academic or emotional pressures without a material resource problem.

exemplars.quote: The rent went up after my shifts were cut.
The empty shelves worried me

codes.label: Embodied vigilance
codes.definition: The writer describes bodily alertness, wakefulness, or a physical stress response.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the body, sleep, shoulders, alertness, or automatic reaction is central to the stress description.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for worry stated only as thought or planning.

exemplars.quote: my shoulders never seem to drop
my body reacted before I knew what happened

codes.label: Practical or social support
codes.definition: Another person, group, or service provides concrete or emotional help that changes the experience.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when dinner, group chat, help-seeking, or shared laughter is described as support.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use when the excerpt only describes self-management with no interpersonal resource.

exemplars.quote: My sister brings dinner twice a week
laughing together helps

codes.label: Self-structured coping
codes.definition: The writer uses routines, boundaries, planning, or checklists to make a demand more manageable.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the excerpt describes a deliberate strategy such as a walk, notifications off, boundary, planning, or checklist.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for relief caused by an external administrative decision alone.

exemplars.quote: A fixed morning walk and turning off notifications
having a sequence makes it feel manageable

codes.label: Resolved or inactive pressure
codes.definition: A previously active stressor is described as ended, reduced, or not currently a crisis.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the writer explicitly says the problem is no longer active or current crisis is absent.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for ongoing mixed strain where the pressure remains active.

exemplars.quote: I am not in crisis now
is no longer active

assignments.rationale: The deadlines compress time and the two in the morning note names sleep disruption.
The post links rent and reduced shifts with a sister's dinners as partial relief.
The writer explicitly says crisis is absent and names routines that make the month ordinary.
Care appointments and a new job compete, while phone calls keep the writer physically tense.
Setting a boundary ended daily messages, though sadness remains.
Shelter timing and a late bus create material and planning demands that consume attention.
The excerpt centers an automatic bodily reaction and sustained alertness after a safe meeting.
The insurance appeal is approved and the prior problem is no longer active.
Empty shelves name material scarcity, and asking for help is presented as emotionally heavy.
Shared humor helps while the broken elevator still creates physical strain.
A demanding move is made manageable through checklist sequencing.
The promotion creates a stream of questions because the writer alone knows the old system.

themes.name: Pressure concentrates through overlapping demands
themes.claim: Several excerpts describe stress as a concentration of demands on time, attention, or basic resources rather than as a single feeling detached from circumstances.
themes.explanation: Academic deadlines, care coordination, shelter timing, food scarcity, and workplace questions each create pressure by narrowing available time or attention. This claim is bounded to the supplied posts and does not infer prevalence beyond them.

evidence.quote: sleeping feels like losing study time
evidence.warrant: Sleep is framed as competing with study obligations.

evidence.quote: there is little attention left for anything else
evidence.warrant: Planning around shelter, bag storage, and phone charging consumes attention.

evidence.quote: every question now reaches me
evidence.warrant: A positive role change creates concentrated workplace demand.

counterevidence.quote: I am not in crisis now
counterevidence.warrant: This excerpt explicitly limits any claim that all posts describe current crisis.

boundary_conditions: Applies only to these fictional posts.
Does not classify writers as chronically stressed people.
Some pressure is resolved or made manageable within the same excerpt.

themes.name: Resources reduce but do not always remove strain
themes.claim: Supportive resources in these excerpts often alter the experience of stress without fully eliminating the underlying pressure.
themes.explanation: Dinner, humor, boundaries, and routines create breathing room, quiet, or manageability. Some excerpts explicitly hold relief and continuing strain together.

evidence.quote: does not fix the bills but gives me one evening when I can breathe
evidence.warrant: The support changes one evening while the bill problem remains.

evidence.quote: the joke and the strain are both real
evidence.warrant: The writer directly preserves both relief and ongoing burden.

evidence.quote: manageable rather than overwhelming
evidence.warrant: Sequencing changes how the demanding move is experienced.

counterevidence.quote: the problem that filled every day then is no longer active
counterevidence.warrant: This is a case of resolution rather than merely partial mitigation.

boundary_conditions: Support is coded from the writer's statement, not assumed from the type of resource.
Relief may be temporary, partial, or complete depending on the excerpt.
No claim is made about which coping strategy is superior.

negative_cases.quote: I am not in crisis now
negative_cases.implication: The packet includes an explicit non-crisis account, so current stress should not be universalized.
Some posts describe past rather than active stressors.

uncertainties: The packet does not state whether help-seeking in DR_E09 succeeds.
The bodily descriptions could reflect immediate stress without implying a durable condition.
alternative_interpretations: DR_E12 could be read as role transition strain rather than only time pressure.
DR_E05 could be primarily about grief over friendship loss, with boundary-setting as secondary.
limitations: Only manifest text in fictional posts was analyzed.
No demographic, diagnostic, or corpus-level claims are warranted.
Source length is short, so theme boundaries remain coarse.

output.research_question: How do these fictional focus-group participants describe disruptions and supports affecting schooling and access to youth health information during a public emergency?
output.analysis_summary: In these fictional focus-group excerpts, schooling and youth health information are shaped by practical constraints: income replacement, transport costs, shared devices, domestic duties, service hours, and privacy concerns. Supports include friends sharing notes, a borrowed tablet and data, peer education, and a quiet appointment. One adult account frames disruption as lost focus, but participant replies reframe it as constrained choice and competing obligations.

codes.label: Income and transport barriers
codes.definition: Money or transport costs interrupt school attendance or return.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the excerpt names household income, replacing income, fare, or transport money as a barrier.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for time conflicts without an explicit money or transport constraint.

exemplars.quote: replacing that income
the bus fare had increased

codes.label: Shared technology limits
codes.definition: Remote learning depends on scarce or shared devices, data, or teacher availability.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the excerpt names a shared phone, tablet, data bundles, delayed lessons, or remote lesson access.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for in-person attendance barriers without a technology component.

exemplars.quote: one phone shared by four people
covered the data bundles

codes.label: Care and domestic time conflict
codes.definition: Household duties or caregiving compete with schooling or clinic access.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when care, water collection, supper preparation, or simultaneous demands on hours are central.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for privacy concerns alone unless they are tied to household duties.

exemplars.quote: caring for two children while my cousin was ill
all demanded the same hours

codes.label: Privacy and reputational risk
codes.definition: Concern about being seen or overheard affects willingness or ability to seek youth health information.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when neighbors, family reporting, main queue privacy, or confidentiality is named.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for service scheduling barriers without visibility or privacy concerns.

exemplars.quote: without neighbors hearing
an older neighbor would see me waiting

codes.label: Peer or family support
codes.definition: Friends, relatives, peer educators, or small groups provide practical access to schooling or information.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a social relation directly supplies notes, devices, data, information, or collaborative learning.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for adult supervision proposed without participant uptake.

exemplars.quote: together we could reconstruct much of the week
I asked a peer educator instead

codes.label: Interest-blame framing challenged
codes.definition: A disruption is framed as lack of focus or interest and then questioned, clarified, or countered by structural explanations.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use for adult blame language, participant rebuttal, or moderator clarification about time conflict rather than interest.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for constraints stated without any focus or interest framing.

exemplars.quote: girls had lost focus during the closure
rather than a lack of interest

assignments.rationale: The participant describes work at an aunt's stall and return to school as replacing household income.
Increased fare limits attendance, while a friend provides copied notes.
Remote lessons are delayed by a phone shared among four people and teacher availability.
The adult attributes closure effects to lost focus and proposes stricter supervision.
The participant rejects the lost-focus account by naming caregiving, transport money, and lack of another caregiver.
Clinic hours overlap with water collection and supper preparation, making a nearby service hard to reach.
A quiet appointment protects privacy and supports willingness to return.
Fear of being seen at the clinic redirects the participant to a peer educator.
Peers pool incomplete notes to reconstruct schoolwork.
An aunt's tablet and data bundles support schooling continuity.
The translated explanation names school, clinic, and home work as demanding the same hours.
The moderator checks whether the issue is time conflict rather than lack of interest.

themes.name: Disruption is practical and simultaneous
themes.claim: Participants describe schooling and clinic access as constrained by practical obligations that occur at the same time, not simply by motivation.
themes.explanation: Income work, transport cost, caregiving, water collection, supper preparation, and schedule conflict appear as concrete barriers. The moderator's clarification and participant rebuttal explicitly resist reducing these barriers to lack of interest.

evidence.quote: Returning was not only a decision about motivation
evidence.warrant: The participant directly rejects motivation as a sufficient explanation.

evidence.quote: Supervision would not create transport money or another person to do the care
evidence.warrant: The participant replaces a supervision frame with transport and care constraints.

evidence.quote: work at home, school, and the clinic all demanded the same hours
evidence.warrant: The excerpt describes simultaneous demands limiting choice.

counterevidence.quote: stricter supervision would solve the problem
counterevidence.warrant: An adult offers an alternate interpretation centered on supervision.

boundary_conditions: This theme reflects the excerpts, not all participants in a real population.
The adult account is preserved as a view in the interaction, not treated as settled explanation.
Translated lines are interpreted only through their provided wording.

themes.name: Access depends on privacy and available intermediaries
themes.claim: Health information and schooling support become reachable when privacy is protected or when peers and family help bridge resource gaps.
themes.explanation: A quiet appointment enables clinic return, a peer educator substitutes for visible waiting, friends reconstruct notes, and a relative supplies technology. These supports are locally effective but unevenly available in the packet.

evidence.quote: that privacy made me willing to return
evidence.warrant: Privacy changes willingness to use the clinic.

evidence.quote: I asked a peer educator instead
evidence.warrant: A peer educator becomes an alternative route to information.

evidence.quote: together we could reconstruct much of the week
evidence.warrant: Peer collaboration helps recover missed school content.

evidence.quote: my schooling continued almost normally
evidence.warrant: Family-provided technology and data enable continuity.

counterevidence.quote: that experience was not shared by several friends in my group
counterevidence.warrant: The participant explicitly limits the reach of this supportive experience.

boundary_conditions: Supports are not assumed available to all participants.
Privacy is coded when stated, not inferred from clinic attendance alone.
The packet does not show long-term educational outcomes.

negative_cases.quote: girls had lost focus during the closure
negative_cases.implication: An adult account attributes disruption to focus, which must be preserved as a competing framing even though participants challenge it.
The packet contains a case of relative continuity, limiting claims that all excerpts show severe school disruption.

uncertainties: The excerpts do not show whether participants ultimately returned to school or maintained clinic contact.
Translated metaphors such as path became narrow are interpreted only through the provided clarification.
alternative_interpretations: AG_E04 could represent concern expressed in limited terms rather than blame alone.
AG_E12 is a moderator clarification, so it may support analytic interpretation without adding participant experience.
limitations: The packet is fictional and not a basis for demographic claims.
Speaker IDs are stable only within source groups.
The analysis cannot estimate how common each barrier is.

output.research_question: What interactional processes move these fictional buyer-seller disputes toward repair or impasse?
output.analysis_summary: Across these fictional buyer-seller dialogues, repair is advanced when parties specify evidence, acknowledge how wording was received, offer bounded options, and translate positions into workable next steps. Impasse emerges where both parties hold fixed procedural demands and decline the other's requested proof or remedy, leading the buyer to exit to platform appeal.

codes.label: Concrete problem claim
codes.definition: A party states the disputed issue and desired remedy in specific terms.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when an excerpt identifies wrong color, late parcel, missing parts, or full refund as the issue or remedy.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for procedural evidence requests that do not state the original complaint.

exemplars.quote: the listing and my order both say red
only a full refund today

codes.label: Evidence request or provision
codes.definition: A party asks for, sends, or proposes photographs, video, serial numbers, tracking, or records to verify the dispute.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use for explicit evidence requests, submitted evidence, or checks against records.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for apologies or options without a verification element.

exemplars.quote: send a photograph of the label
confirm each part against the photographs

codes.label: Accountability for wording
codes.definition: A party recognizes how prior wording or format was interpreted and repairs the interactional meaning.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when an excerpt names dismissive wording, accusation, hostile interpretation, or explains intended meaning.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for logistical explanations without attention to how communication was received.

exemplars.quote: I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive
I now see that you were listing the missing parts

codes.label: Bounded repair offer
codes.definition: A party offers a specific conditional remedy, timeline, or acceptable resolution.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a turn proposes prepaid return, replacement, inquiry, refund condition, missing parts, or a date.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for demands that leave no negotiable path unless they include an actionable condition accepted by the other party.

exemplars.quote: refund if there is no scan in three days
would accept the missing parts instead of a full refund

codes.label: Conditional acceptance
codes.definition: A party accepts a proposed path if a specific condition is met.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a party says a proposed return, waiting period, missing parts, or inquiry number would resolve or be acceptable.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for fixed refusal or platform exit.

exemplars.quote: A prepaid return and the red kettle would resolve this for me
I can wait three more days if you send the inquiry number

codes.label: Procedural impasse
codes.definition: The exchange becomes stuck because parties repeat incompatible evidence or remedy demands.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a turn refuses further evidence, refuses refund discussion without evidence, or names repeated demand and exits.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for conditional evidence requests that are embedded in a repair path.

exemplars.quote: I will not discuss a refund without it
we are repeating the same demand

assignments.rationale: The buyer specifies the color mismatch and asks for replacement or refund.
The seller requests label evidence and conditionally offers to cover the return.
The buyer reports sending a photograph and states what would resolve the issue.
The buyer names lateness and identifies the seller's prior wording as dismissive.
The seller apologizes for wording, gives tracking information, and offers inquiry or refund timing.
The buyer accepts waiting if the seller sends the inquiry number.
The seller revises an accusation reading into a missing-parts reading.
The buyer clarifies intent, offers photographs, and accepts missing parts rather than full refund.
The seller accepts the path and will verify parts against photographs before shipping.
The buyer makes a fixed same-day refund demand and refuses another video.
The seller requires a new serial-number video and refuses refund discussion without it.
The buyer names repeated demands and exits to platform appeal.

themes.name: Repair develops through verifiable next steps
themes.claim: In three dialogues, movement toward repair occurs when concrete claims are paired with evidence practices and specific next actions.
themes.explanation: The wrong-color, late-parcel, and missing-parts disputes each move beyond complaint when parties request or provide evidence and define what would resolve the problem. The interactional process is sequential rather than a trait of either role.

evidence.quote: If we shipped the wrong color, I will cover the return
evidence.warrant: The seller links verification to a remedy.

evidence.quote: I can wait three more days if you send the inquiry number
evidence.warrant: The buyer accepts a timed path with a concrete condition.

evidence.quote: I will confirm each part against the photographs before shipping them
evidence.warrant: The seller turns the buyer's evidence offer into a fulfillment step.

counterevidence.quote: I will not discuss a refund without it
counterevidence.warrant: Here the evidence requirement blocks discussion rather than enabling repair.

boundary_conditions: The claim applies to the fictional dialogues supplied here.
Repair is inferred from movement toward agreed next steps, not from confirmed final delivery.
Buyer and seller roles both contribute to repair in different turns.

themes.name: Misread tone can be repaired when named
themes.claim: Two dialogues show that naming and revising perceived tone helps shift the exchange from relational friction back to the substantive dispute.
themes.explanation: A seller apologizes for wording that sounded dismissive, and another seller revises a reading of directness as accusation. A buyer also clarifies a numbered list as clear rather than hostile. These repairs matter because they open space for timed inquiry or missing-parts remedies.

evidence.quote: I am sorry my short wording sounded dismissive
evidence.warrant: The seller acknowledges the buyer's interpretation of prior wording.

evidence.quote: I now see that you were listing the missing parts
evidence.warrant: The seller corrects an accusation reading.

evidence.quote: clear, not hostile
evidence.warrant: The buyer clarifies intent and pairs it with a repair option.

counterevidence.quote: I will not provide another video because I already sent one last week
counterevidence.warrant: This turn does not repair relational meaning and instead fixes a limit.

boundary_conditions: Tone repair is coded only when explicitly named in the dialogue.
The packet does not show whether apologies are accepted beyond the immediate next turn.
This is an interactional claim, not a cultural or personality claim.

themes.name: Fixed reciprocal demands create impasse
themes.claim: The fourth dialogue moves toward impasse when buyer and seller each maintain incompatible procedural demands and the buyer exits the conversation.
themes.explanation: The buyer asks for only a full refund and refuses another video; the seller requires a new video and refuses refund discussion without it. The final turn names repetition and moves to platform appeal, marking a shift away from dyadic repair.

evidence.quote: I will accept only a full refund today
evidence.warrant: The buyer states a fixed remedy demand.

evidence.quote: Our policy requires a new video with the serial number visible
evidence.warrant: The seller makes refund discussion contingent on new evidence.

evidence.quote: I am ending this conversation and using the platform appeal
evidence.warrant: The buyer exits the direct interaction.

counterevidence.quote: open an inquiry today or refund if there is no scan in three days
counterevidence.warrant: Another dialogue shows policy or tracking information being paired with options rather than deadlock.

boundary_conditions: This theme is based on one dialogue, though it contrasts with other dialogues.
The platform appeal may later resolve the dispute, but that is outside the supplied excerpts.
The analysis does not evaluate which party is correct about policy or evidence.

negative_cases.quote: I will not discuss a refund without it
negative_cases.implication: Evidence requirements can become a barrier when not paired with a mutually acceptable path.

negative_cases.quote: I will not provide another video
negative_cases.implication: Buyer refusal also contributes to impasse, so the stuck process is reciprocal in the supplied sequence.

uncertainties: The excerpts do not show whether repair offers are completed after the final turns.
Policy correctness and prior evidence quality cannot be assessed from the supplied text.
alternative_interpretations: KO_E11 could be read as legitimate procedure rather than stonewalling, but in sequence it contributes to impasse.
KO_E04's complaint about dismissive wording could be a substantive service issue as well as tone repair.
limitations: Only four short fictional dialogues are analyzed.
No national, platform-wide, or buyer/seller trait claims are warranted.
Sequential conclusions are limited to the displayed turns.

output.research_question: How do partners in these fictional everyday conversations negotiate support, understanding, and boundaries during disclosure?
output.analysis_summary: In these fictional dyadic conversations, disclosure is negotiated through questions, requests for the preferred kind of support, clarification of ambiguous signals, and explicit boundaries. Support becomes more fitting when the listener asks or explains rather than assuming, while the disclosing partner often refines what they need: listening before advice, plain speech instead of guessing, or a cue that silence means thinking.

codes.label: Vulnerable disclosure
codes.definition: A speaker reveals uncertainty, fear, ambivalence, or a concern they have not fully shared.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a speaker discloses fear about artwork, job uncertainty, reluctance about a trip, or an assumption of disapproval.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for a listener's response unless it contains their own disclosure.

exemplars.quote: I am afraid the work looks childish
I do not know whether to leave my job

codes.label: Inquiry before evaluation
codes.definition: A listener responds with questions that invite the speaker to define meaning, safety, or difficulty before judging or advising.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use for questions that ask what motivated, would feel safe, or is making a decision hard.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for direct advice or assumed interpretation.

exemplars.quote: what would feel safe enough to share first
ask what is making the decision hard

codes.label: Premature advice
codes.definition: A listener offers action steps before the speaker has asked for planning help.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the response moves directly to resume, manager contact, or options despite a request to say worries aloud.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for suggestions that follow an explicit invitation for advice.

exemplars.quote: update your resume tonight and call my manager tomorrow

codes.label: Support preference stated
codes.definition: A speaker names what kind of support or response would be useful, safe, or not useful at the moment.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a speaker asks for listening, asks for a question, identifies a safer sharing step, or requests a thinking cue.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for general disclosure with no stated support preference.

exemplars.quote: I could show you the small landscape
Right now, could you listen

codes.label: Ambiguous signal clarified
codes.definition: A speaker explains that a laugh, silence, or prior response had a different meaning than the partner inferred.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when the interaction turns on clarifying laughter, silence, or what a response sounded like.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for clear preferences stated without prior ambiguity.

exemplars.quote: I thought the laugh meant you liked the idea
I did not realize the silence sounded like judgment

codes.label: Boundary or preference made explicit
codes.definition: A speaker moves from indirectness or uncertainty to a clear limit, preference, or next-time request.
codes.inclusion_rule: Use when a speaker plainly refuses a trip form, asks for listening over advice, or requests a cue about silence.
codes.exclusion_rule: Do not use for exploratory questions unless they result in a stated boundary or preference.

exemplars.quote: not another long drive this month
saying that you are thinking would stop me

assignments.rationale: The speaker discloses returning to painting and fear that the work looks childish.
The listener asks about motivation and what would feel safe before evaluating the work.
The speaker says the question is easier than praise and proposes a safe first share.
The speaker discloses job uncertainty and says they need to voice worries before planning.
The listener moves directly into resume and manager advice.
The speaker postpones advice and asks for listening plus a question about difficulty.
The speaker discloses the laugh masked reluctance and clarifies its meaning.
The listener states how they interpreted the laugh and asks not to plan around a guess.
The speaker plainly states wanting time together but not another long drive this month.
The speaker discloses interpreting the partner's silence as disapproval.
The listener explains the silence as thinking and recognizes it sounded like judgment.
The speaker says the explanation changes the silence and requests a next-time cue.

themes.name: Questions calibrate support
themes.claim: Support is negotiated more precisely when partners ask about meaning, safety, or difficulty before offering evaluation or action.
themes.explanation: In the painting exchange, a question creates an easier path to sharing. In the job exchange, the speaker corrects premature advice by asking for listening and inquiry. The theme does not imply questions are always sufficient; it is tied to these turns.

evidence.quote: What made you choose painting again
evidence.warrant: The listener invites context rather than immediate judgment.

evidence.quote: That question is easier than being told it is good
evidence.warrant: The speaker explicitly values inquiry over reassurance.

evidence.quote: Right now, could you listen and ask what is making the decision hard?
evidence.warrant: The speaker specifies listening and inquiry as the desired support.

counterevidence.warrant: The listener's advice is intended as support but arrives before the requested listening.

boundary_conditions: Applies to the displayed conversations only.
Does not diagnose either partner's communication style.
Advice may become useful later because the speaker says may want those ideas later.

themes.name: Ambiguity is repaired through explicit meaning
themes.claim: Partners negotiate understanding by naming how ambiguous cues were interpreted and then replacing guesses with clearer statements.
themes.explanation: A laugh is first read as liking the trip and then clarified as masking reluctance; silence is read as disapproval and then explained as thoughtfulness. The repair depends on both the interpretation and the correction being spoken.

evidence.quote: I thought the laugh meant you liked the idea
evidence.warrant: The listener identifies the mistaken inference from laughter.

evidence.quote: Then I will say it plainly
evidence.warrant: The speaker shifts from indirectness to explicit preference.

evidence.quote: I did not realize the silence sounded like judgment
evidence.warrant: The listener recognizes how silence was interpreted.

evidence.quote: Knowing that changes the silence for me
evidence.warrant: The speaker reports that the explanation changes the meaning of the cue.

counterevidence.quote: I was also trying not to say that I do not want to go
counterevidence.warrant: Before clarification, the speaker withholds the plain preference.

boundary_conditions: The theme concerns interactional repair, not stable honesty or sensitivity traits.
The excerpts do not show whether future cues are adopted.
Only laughter and silence are evidenced here.

themes.name: Boundaries preserve connection while limiting action
themes.claim: Several disclosures pair a desire for connection with a boundary about what should happen next.
themes.explanation: The speakers do not simply accept or reject support; they define acceptable forms: show one small painting, voice worries before planning, spend time together without a long drive, and ask for a thinking cue next time.

evidence.quote: show you the small landscape and explain why I kept it
evidence.warrant: The speaker chooses a bounded first share.

evidence.quote: say the worries aloud before I make a plan
evidence.warrant: The speaker sets a sequence for support before action.

evidence.quote: I want time together, but not another long drive this month
evidence.warrant: The speaker preserves connection while limiting the proposed activity.

counterevidence.quote: update your resume tonight and call my manager tomorrow
counterevidence.warrant: This response moves to action before the speaker's boundary is restated.

boundary_conditions: The theme does not claim all boundaries are resolved or accepted beyond the excerpted turn.
Connection is inferred only where the quote preserves sharing, listening, or time together.
No stable partner roles are assigned.

negative_cases.quote: You should update your resume tonight and call my manager tomorrow.
negative_cases.implication: Not all support attempts begin with inquiry; advice can arrive before the discloser is ready for planning.

negative_cases.quote: I was also trying not to say that I do not want to go.
negative_cases.implication: Disclosure can initially be indirect, so plain boundaries may emerge only after interactional clarification.

uncertainties: The excerpts end before showing whether requested future behavior changes occur.
The emotional weight of each disclosure can only be inferred from the words provided.
alternative_interpretations: CA_E05 could be read as practical care, not merely premature advice, because it offers options.
CA_E11's silence could be experienced as supportive reflection by one partner and judgment by the other.
limitations: The packet is fictional and limited to four short dyadic sequences.
No diagnosis or stable personality attribution is warranted.
Themes are based on sequential turns, not independent reports across broader contexts.
